rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child: both are letters to the Speaker transmitting military appropriation recommendations for a specified fiscal year, quantify the requested authority, explain its principal military uses, and connect the spending to a broader national-security program and international peace. The child greatly expands this framework, but the shared opening formula and parallel budgetary-security structure are material rather than merely topical. C10 has an even closer transmission formula but is too brief to match as much of the child's substantive organization; C20 similarly combines an appropriation request with an extended free-world defense rationale, but concerns foreign military assistance rather than the Department of Defense's own military budget.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Sir: I transmit herewith for the consideration of the Congress my budget recommendations for the military functions of the Department of Defense for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1952.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As one element in building up our strength to the necessary level, I am transmitting herewith for the consideration of the Congress a draft of a proposed provision ... in the form of an amendment to the Budget for the fiscal year 1949.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared congressional budget-transmission formula tied to a specified fiscal year and national-security buildup.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The funds I am recommending today will finance the following elements of our armed strength. ... For the Army ... The Navy ... The Marine Corps ... The Air Force ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: While almost every part of our military program will be affected by the proposed increase, the additions may be grouped in five categories: First ... added military personnel ... Second ... aircraft ... Third ... maintenance and operation ... Fourth ... procurement and production programs ... Fifth ... other requirements ...
shared_material.explanation: Both move from the aggregate request to an organized accounting of military personnel, procurement, operations, equipment, and research requirements.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This budget estimate represents, therefore, but one of the parts of our national security program. ... In money terms, by far the largest part of this total security program is the cost of building up our own military strength.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: To accomplish this objective, a limited increase in our national security program is required. ... The proposed appropriations are intended to round out and balance our national security program.
shared_material.explanation: The military appropriation is framed in both documents as one component of a broader, balanced national-security program directed toward peace and international responsibilities.
